cases.requirement_description: existing `device_status` Tools/list has the same single Tool, no hidden sensitive Tools/Resources, and exact v1 status fields.
Kotlin NativeLocalStatus JSON has runtime `android`, schema version 1, zero device IDs and false Accessibility/privileged flags.
official Kotlin SDK over loopback responds to a valid Tool call with expected result and bounded response; unknown Tool is denied.
N2 Activity only serves while explicitly started; Home/onStop releases its own endpoint and does not start N3.
N3 foreground mode survives Home with correct notification, then actual UI/notification Stop removes listener and service.
mutate an isolated golden fixture field to prove regression detection, restore it, and show no physical Android device command.
a fake approved local caller using correct Origin/Host/context is recognized under the planned policy, without exposing new sensitive Tools.
localhost connection by another process/app with no authenticated identity cannot list/call future sensitive Tools.
wrong/missing Origin, attacker-controlled Host, unexpected path and preflight spoof are rejected before sensitive handlers.
replayed request, cross-origin preflight, malformed headers, giant body and connection flood have bounded/typed denials.
a process restart/second listener cannot inherit stale caller authorization; identity is not inferred from loopback IP.
exact baseline status still works under reviewed compatibility policy; no unreviewed public bind or private key leaks.
Activity start/stop and N3 opt-in FGS start/stop follow distinct explicit state transitions with a single port owner.
second Activity or FGS listener fails closed while the first owns the endpoint, with truthful user-facing error.
Ktor shutdown exception plus still-bound socket leaves port-owner state UNKNOWN and blocks a second startup.
port closure/readiness marker mismatch or timeout never releases ownership or falsely reports service healthy.
Android API30/33/34/36 emulator Home, orientation, notification denial, actual Stop and process death never auto-resurrect.
Activity/FGS contention, rapid Stop/Start and retry produce at most one listener, no orphan notification/port.
known Android API+permission tuples map to explicit granted/denied/unknown/not-applicable states without inventing a grant.
no Accessibility, MediaProjection, QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, device admin, Root or storage permission appears in current actual manifest.
Android 11 lacks Android 13 runtime notification grant semantics while API33+ refusal prevents current FGS start.
user revokes notification/app permission while service runs; readiness updates and sensitive operations deny after recheck.
missing Android system service/API or OEM exception returns unsupported/unknown with no permission prompt loop.
native permission-status output discloses no secrets, private settings or full package list and is versioned.
an app-owned synthetic binary becomes an opaque handle with MIME, size, SHA-256 and bounded expiry.
a guessed handle, caller-forged URI, symlink/path traversal or another-app private file is denied.
oversized artifact/disk-full/private-directory permission error leaves no trusted partial file or sensitive log.
concurrent duplicate IDs and crash during atomic commit cannot overwrite another artifact or publish partial content.
FGS Stop/process restart/expiry destroys or reconciles artifacts according to explicit retention; no orphan.
raw screenshots, tokens, account data and capture frames never appear in MCP JSON, normal logcat or audit.
representative Build.VERSION/SDK/ABI/app Build values normalize to a versioned typed snapshot.
hardware/device serial, advertising ID, Android ID, network MAC and other persistent IDs are absent.
missing/unexpected OEM Build fields or unusual ABI lists return partial/unavailable, not invented defaults.
API30/33/34/36 snapshot adapter respects actual API availability and supported type/units.
malformed Kotlin codec, oversized model/version string and unsupported UTF-8 are bounded/redacted.
public sensitive profile stays denied without N0.b gate, even if a synthetic service can read Build locally.
fake BatteryManager, storage free bytes, display metrics and connectivity report consistent units/timestamps.
permission-denied network/location data, offline connectivity and missing service return explicit partial/unavailable.
very large/negative battery/storage counters and OEM missing fields never overflow or become plausible readings.
Android API30/33/34/36 tests check the correct availability of display/storage/network APIs without using privileged stats.
event/refresh on FGS Stop does not retain old device state or start background subscriptions automatically.
MCP denied/safe responses omit SSIDs, nearby device IDs, precise location and other unrelated sensitive state.
running Activity or FGS reports correct application/process service mode, uptime and permitted readiness.
process crash/FGS kill, notification Stop and explicit user Stop are distinguished; stopped never reports healthy.
failed bind, cancelled start and readiness-oracle collision yield typed error with no second port owner.
retry after process death/Android reboot never automatically starts a background service (START_NOT_STICKY).
remote/unpaired clients cannot obtain detailed stacktrace, PID list, private filesystem or app credentials.
HTTP Tool call with fake lifecycle states preserves baseline status/v1 errors and bounded JSON.
unauthenticated default tools/list only advertises approved minimal status, with no screenshot/package/UI Tool.
a fake authorized capability profile exposes only explicitly allowed focused Tools with correct Kotlin SDK JSON Schemas.
unsupported Android API or revoked permission hides/denies Tool independently of model-supplied `approved=true`.
caller profile switch, reconnect and process restart cannot reuse stale permission/Origin context.
tools/call errors and structuredContent map consistent success/partial/denial; metadata never mislabels mutating actions read-only.
baseline three Host Tools are untouched; Native only changes its own registry and v1 compatibility is preserved.
known PackageManager visible packages return bounded, sorted permitted subset with explicit filter notes.
hidden packages are not silently treated as nonexistent; report visibility restrictions on API30/33/34/36.
unexpected broad QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES permission or privileged cross-user enumeration is denied by policy.
malformed package metadata, huge app lists and slow PackageManager calls produce bounded partial/error results.
unpaired local callers cannot enumerate visible application packages via MCP despite service-local access.
package results contain no account tokens/signature private keys or unrelated other-app permissions.
explicit visible package ID resolves versionName/versionCode, certificate digest and exported metadata allowed by API.
unknown, hidden, disabled, uninstalled and wrong-user packages yield distinct typed not-found/visibility errors.
invalid package names, control characters, huge labels and model-provided filesystem paths denied.
API30/33/34/36 PackageManager field behavior checked without broad visibility/hidden-API bypass.
request after package uninstall/disable or lost caller grant is revalidated, no stale cached elevation.
tools/call output versioned, capped and protected from unauthorized local/remote origins.
allowlisted explicit app/activity Intent resolves a visible/exported target to a deterministic launch **plan**.
implicit/broadcast/deep-link unknown Intent, nonexported component and wrong user are denied before launch.
arbitrary extras/URI tricks, oversized payload, intent flags/selector escalation and shell text are rejected.
foreground/background launch restrictions and API30/33/34/36 support accurately reported.
duplicate plan is idempotent, but actual launch still requires separate user grant and cannot auto-repeat.
mocked ActivityManager/PackageManager asserts zero launches, permission changes or task switches.
MediaProjection unavailable/no user consent yields denied and a truthful user-visible consent **plan**.
Android API34/36 per-session MediaProjection token cannot be reused, forged or treated as a durable credential.
API30/33 versus API34/36 foreground-service type and Android manifest requirements checked; no automatic manifest permission expansion.
user refusal, lock/screen-off, activity destruction and FGS Stop revoke capture readiness immediately.
unrelated process/Origin/caller cannot invoke a future sensitive capture Tool via loopback.
default built APK remains within approved current Manifest permission allowlist, no capture started by synthetic consent flag.
with real disposable-emulator user consent and authenticated fake caller, one accepted projection frame becomes private hashed artifact.
missing/refused/revoked consent, locked/secure window and unpaired caller result in denial, no image artifact.
frame dimensions, pixel buffer, MIME, file size and timeout are strictly capped; malformed frame is rejected.
Android API30/33/34/36 projection grant lifecycle tested under actual emulator only when permission-gated test APK available.
Stop/projection callback/process death immediately stops capture and releases image readers, buffers and handles.
no frame bytes in normal Tool JSON, logs or status; absent required permission keeps production Tool disabled.
a user-consented disposable-emulator capture starts finite recording with explicit duration/resolution/size limits.
unauthenticated caller, stale/reused consent, API34/36 token reuse and background-only request are denied.
cancellation, user Stop, MediaProjection.onStop and FGS process death release encoder/surface and delete partial file.
repeated start or two overlapping captures cannot reuse one MediaProjection token or create silent background recording.
disk full, dropped frames, oversized output and codec failure return partial/uncertain, never forged complete video.
recording artifacts have short private TTL and hash; Android permission Manifest does not silently expand.
Accessibility disabled by default with accurate permission/use-case status; no hidden service activation.
user denying Accessibility enablement keeps UI inspection/action functions unavailable; no direct Settings grant.
an absent Android service declaration cannot be interpreted as permitted from fabricated model args.
API30/33/34/36 Accessibility restrictions and applicability of user-facing purpose are explicitly tested/fail closed.
service revocation/stop/lock-screen and fake hostile caller clear capabilities; no stale approved UI nodes.
production Manifest and default tools/list show no privileged Accessibility Tool/permission without reviewed feature gate.
approved fake Accessibility tree emits bounded node roles/visible structure, focus and stable ephemeral handles only.
password fields, secure/locked screen, other-app private text and hidden window are masked or inaccessible.
no service, revoked grant, stale node epoch and unrelated caller return typed denial without returning old tree.
enormous/deep/cyclic node hierarchy is capped by size/depth/node count with partial annotation.
Android API30/33/34/36 scoped hierarchy reading checked on user-consented disposable emulator where available.
read Tree Tool never dispatches gestures, changes UI state or exposes broader Accessibility actions.
typed tap/swipe/scroll/key intent creates a deterministic plan bound to current focused window and ephemeral node epoch.
out-of-range coordinates, wrong display rotation, unknown key/gesture and arbitrary shell text are denied.
stale node/window, unavailable Accessibility, locked screen and no caller authentication deny dispatch.
duplicate plan has stable digest but actual UI gesture is marked non-idempotent and cannot auto-replay after timeout.
cancellation before dispatch causes zero injected events; cancellation after dispatch reports uncertain rather than undoing input.
default Native Tool never executes a gesture or broad Accessibility action from an `approved=true` model field.
test runner confirms exact known emulator serial, `ro.kernel.qemu=1`, expected API/ABI and boot completion **before** any input.
connected physical USB tablet, mismatched SDK API and unknown emulator serial are rejected with zero tap/key dispatch.
genuine disposable API30/33/34/36 instrumentation test sends bounded tap/swipe/key and verifies expected UI state only on its own test app.
stale UI hierarchy after rotation, app restart or dialog transition causes reinspection, never blind repeat.
timeout, ADB disconnect and test runner kill produce an uncertain operation with no fallback to real Android.
test cleanup stops only owned test Activity/AVD state, not another AVD or physical Native service.
actual user-provided ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT URI grant is represented by an opaque scoped handle with exact access mode.
model-forged content URI, wrong authority/provider, revoked/expired grant and unchecked file paths are denied.
permissions for read versus write and persistable versus one-time URI grants are kept distinct.
Activity result absent/cancelled/invalid, provider kill or provider throwing returns typed denied/partial.
API30/33/34/36 SAF picker/grant behavior is checked without requesting MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE.
no other app's files or broad `/sdcard` directory becomes accessible merely by loading a document URI string.
user-chosen readable SAF source is copied as a bounded private artifact with correct MIME/size/SHA-256.
URI without READ grant, revoked permissions, symbolic provider alias and wrong ContentProvider process fail closed.
cancellation, disk full, oversized content and broken provider stream leave no trusted partial file.
duplicate export request has one stable artifact handle; process death/restart never restores stale grant implicitly.
API30/33/34/36 picker result and denied/cancelled user choice produce accurate code paths in disposable emulator.
no raw document bytes, sensitive file path, account identifier or personally identifying content in public MCP errors/logs.
authorized user-selected WRITE URI and trusted hash-matching artifact produce an atomic/import **plan**.
read-only/revoked URI, wrong provider, outside-scope destination or forged write grant are denied.
oversized payload/stream failure/provider crash cleans partial content or reports uncertainty without falsely claiming atomicity.
duplicate import request or stale artifact digest never silently overwrites another document.
emulator user cancellation at picker and process death before/after dispatch are separately classified.
default public Tool is disabled until real user URI grant/caller auth, and never writes an arbitrary local/system path.
allowed non-sensitive battery/display/connectivity status is read with exact Android API and permission metadata.
location, microphone, contacts and notification content remain unavailable without specific actual runtime consent.
model-requested background polling/continuous sensor tracking cannot enable a persistent surveillance loop.
API30/33/34/36 permission changes, sensor unsupported, disabled location provider and revoked grant return typed unavailable.
high-rate sensor events are bounded and unsubscribed on FGS Stop, Activity destruction and client disconnect.
public JSON omits nearby IDs, precise coordinates, notification text and unrelated sensitive platform data.
synthetic app-owned exception/ANR produces a bounded structured report with Native app version, uptime and code.
failure in a different app's process cannot be read through unrestricted system Logcat or hidden privileged APIs.
exception message containing user tokens, addresses and secrets is redacted from public MCP response and ordinary logs.
crash of FGS while report is being recorded leaves accurate incomplete/restart state, not retroactive success.
report/artifact retention expiry and deletion are enforced after reboot/process restart without leaking orphan files.
no sensitive diagnostics become accessible to unauthenticated localhost process/Origin.
sampled own-process memory/cpu/event latency values use stable units, time and app process identity.
attempting global kernel/perfetto/root/systemwide profiling from a regular app returns explicit unsupported/denied.
API30/33/34/36 process API and permission availability yield truthful partial/unsupported values.
background FGS Stop, app sleep and process restart clear stale counters rather than reporting healthy sample streams.
long/high-frequency sample requests are rate/buffer capped and cancelled on demand.
no ungranted app/process identifiers or raw private backtraces are returned in model-visible status.
bounded diagnostic event is stored with monotonic ID/timestamp, origin and allowed sensitivity classification.
duplicate request/late ack cannot insert a second event or advance cursor incorrectly; slow consumer receives bounded pages.
process death and FGS restart reopen/reconcile pending event state without inventing a completed subscriber delivery.
expiry, capacity overflow and backpressure drop events honestly with counters; no unbounded in-memory queue.
invalid/foreign cursor, revoked caller and invalid owner cannot access a prior user's diagnostics.
Stop/unsubscribe closes listeners/threads/files and erases sensitive expired artifacts per policy.
Host ADB alive and Native service dead returns a read-only Host fallback suggestion with distinct provider identity.
Host offline but Native user-started service alive provides only capabilities actually permitted to Native.
both available and both unavailable cases report distinct status/provenance without silently choosing first provider.
native instance reinstall, boot-epoch change, USB disconnect and serial reuse invalidate stale pairing/fallback refs.
loss of Native write lease cannot enable Host APK install, root, Accessibility or fallback UI write.
fake Host/Native MCP interaction has typed unknown/denied errors, no real USB/physical device operation.
fresh installation creates a private instance identity and public verification key independent of Android serial/MAC.
uninstall/reinstall or app data clear rotates install identity and invalidates old Host binding.
private key material cannot be returned by Tools/list, tools/call, status or logcat and is stored under app sandbox protections.
device reboot/FGS restart does not silently change install identity, but invalidates transient auth challenges.
corrupted/denied key storage and concurrent first-start identity creation fail closed without duplicating ownership.
a model-provided identity string or ADB serial cannot impersonate a signed, registered installation.
deterministic fake signed nonce challenge binds versioned Host identity, exact Native instance and boot epoch.
replay, wrong key, tampered digest, stale timestamp, mismatched Origin/Host and cross-device challenge are denied.
unauthenticated 127.0.0.1 caller may receive minimal status but no device data/capture/action through mock authorization.
service restart/USB reconnect cannot reuse previous transient challenge or treat tunnel presence as identity.
malformed/oversized packet, 100 concurrent challenge attempts and clock rollback remain bounded.
absent jointly accepted shared protocol leaves Native pairing production route disabled, not guessed compatible.
monotonic fenced lease token/high-water mark persists across Native FGS process restart and app lifecycle.
stale token/duplicate action digest/wrong Host identity and reused nonce are rejected prior to mutation.
boot epoch/reinstall/clock rollback invalidate existing lease and cannot reset high-water mark without new pairing.
crash or disk-full during persistence results in denied/uncertain state, not a valid unpersisted grant.
two concurrent accessors to persistent lease record have one atomic winner and no high-water regression.
default Native MCP status remains nonprivileged; no real device-mutation executor is connected to fake fencing logic.
synthetic Host A vs Host B concurrent acquire for same target/plan yields only one active authorized lease.
wrong Host renewal, expired TTL, stale fence, repeated release and out-of-order request fail closed.
user stops Native FGS while lease held; Host receives uncertain/unavailable and cannot force device action.
Native app process death during an action leaves durable ambiguous receipt, no blind replay after restart.
mismatched Host/Native package or future schema version fails compatibility gate without ignoring unknown required fields.
fake dual runtime tests prove no real Host CLI process, physical ADB mutation or public unauthenticated listener is used.
default actual Kotlin tools/list exposes no installation/gesture/system-setting write Tool to unpaired caller.
fake model-supplied `approved=true` or stale signed action does not bypass caller/permission/lease checks.
even with a synthetic lease, missing true Android runtime consent denies Accessibility/MediaProjection/PackageInstaller actions.
mutation Tool metadata accurately describes non-idempotent, potentially destructive effects and honest disabled state.
replay after uncertain result cannot execute duplicate UI gesture/install, and no action runs after user Stop.
APK Manifest contains no extra privileged service/permission; all real mutating handlers remain inactive until independent reviewed enabling PR.
a validated trusted APK artifact digest/package/ABI yields a deterministic user-mediated PackageInstaller **plan**.
unsigned/bad certificate, wrong target SDK, missing artifact and arbitrary file URI inputs are rejected.
caller claims of `installWithoutPrompt`, `approved=true` or broad installation permission fail closed.
API30/33/34/36 user consent/unknown-sources policy is represented accurately, never treated as granted.
cancel/replay of a plan never initiates installation or leaves a trusted open install session.
default Native public Tool remains disabled for install, even when mock installer service is available.
a verified disposable emulator can open an Android-mediated user-confirmation flow for a signed test APK only.
user refusal or canceled installer UI causes no installed package and accurately reports denied/cancelled.
physical ADB serial, unrelated emulator, invalid qemu/API and unapproved app package are rejected **before** install.
process death, lost foreground and installer session abandonment clean up test session artifacts without silent retry.
Android API30/33/34/36 emulator paths verify platform consent/unknown-sources differences when relevant; unavailable matrix is blocked.
test harness never enables silent privileged physical APK installation or broad REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES without independent policy gate.
an exact exported Activity explicitly approved by user/authorized caller can be launched in safe disposable emulator.
non-exported, unknown, off-user, locked-screen or implicit Intent to another app is denied.
background-start restrictions and Android API30/33/34/36 are respected; no hidden start-from-FGS bypass.
duplicate launch/non-idempotent task transition records action ID, no blind rerun after ambiguous timeout.
user/Origin revocation or FGS Stop between authorization and dispatch prevents execution.
initial status-only app retains unchanged behavior, no foreign package force-stop or broad shell command added.
explicit user Start after legitimate Stop reclaims the port only after verified shutdown and fresh readiness proof.
Android process kill, reboot and START_NOT_STICKY do not silently resurrect N3 or open its endpoint.
unreleased port, stale owner, failed notification stop and second owner collision fail closed with accurate UI status.
API30/33/34/36 notification permission refusal and foreground-service restrictions tested on verified AVDs.
service restart invalidates outstanding sensitive capture sessions, caller challenges and active leases.
no wake-lock/battery exemption, boot receiver, always-on background agent or external port introduced by recovery.
non-DeviceOwner ordinary Native app reports managed device features unsupported without provisioning.
fake verified DeviceOwner state reports supported capability names but defaults to **plan-only** for policy changes.
model-controlled Device Admin/Owner role string cannot self-provision, elevate privileges or install admin policies.
API30/33/34/36 DevicePolicyManager restrictions are reflected accurately; OEM differences yield unsupported.
attempts to wipe, lock, change account/policy or silent install are rejected with zero OS side effects.
Default Manifest/registered Tools remain nonadministrative and no real enterprise provisioning is performed.
ordinary Native APK reports root/Bootloader/ROM flashing unavailable and explains Host-supervised alternative.
no unrestricted `su`, ADB shell, OEM Fastboot or raw partition Tool appears in Native tools/list.
fake Android crash/unbootable mode correctly marks Native service unavailable, not remotely recoverable via local APK.
invalid Host identity or missing ADB/Fastboot authorization never triggers new elevated privileges as a fallback.
model attempts to bypass lockscreen/integrity, erase data or unlock Bootloader yield typed denied/unsupported.
safe recovery **plan** includes physical-owner confirmation requirements and no actual device/reboot/flash command executed.
